newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will talk today with thousands of villagers staging a sit-in outside Government House. More than 20,000 villagers from 10 northeastern provinces have streamed into Bangkok by bus, truck and train since Friday to protest outside Government House. They have vowed to remain there until their demands are met. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Social Action Party leader Montree Pongpanit has announced he will step down from the committee looking into land encroachment and as vice chairman of the New Bangkok International Airport Co - in apparent dissent against Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. Montree says he will this week inform Chavalit that he will not accept either position because his portfolio has nothing to do with such issues. (THE NATION)

- Several laboratory technicians, tasked with analysing narcotics samples seized by police, have quit their jobs after receiving threats from drug traffickers and their relatives. These technicians are also required to appear in court to present their findings in cases brought against drug suspects. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) is set to promote the country as the region's shopping centre. The objective of the campaign, which will cost 100 million baht in the first year of its operation, is to make Thailand the shopping hub of Southeast Asia by 1999 and in Asia and the Pacific by the following year. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand will shortly consider opening an internal enquiry into the alleged mishandling by some officials in the collapse of Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC), says the governor of the bank. The decision will be made after the central bank has completed the rescue plans for BBC. The medium-sized bank was rescued by the government last year. The central bank has confirmed a bad debt level of 50 billion baht. (THE NATION)

- The Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT) will scrap its revenue-sharing arrangements with pager operators and liberalise the industry this year. Private operation of pager services licensed by the TOT will be approved providing they meet conditions being drafted. (BANGKOK POST)
